slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Choosing a strategy: list what is given, mark it on the figure, and look for the third part. Shared sides give equal sides (reflexive). Crossing lines give vertical angles. Midpoints and bisectors give equal pieces. Isosceles triangles give equal base angles.

Then pick the test that fits: SSS, SAS (angle between the sides) or ASA (side between the angles). Never SSA or AAA. Finish with CPCTC if you need a part, not just the triangles.

slides.title: Check yourself
slides.html: Given AB = CD and BC = DA in quadrilateral ABCD. Which two triangles and which test show angle B = angle D?
slides.reveal: Triangles ABC and CDA share AC; with AB = CD and BC = DA they are congruent by SSS, so angle B = angle D by CPCTC.
